role: ImportDataView extension holding the import logic: file picking, off-main read/format sniff/parse, single-recording analysis and save, Elite HRV summary batch import, Emuqu multi-session batch import with full re-analysis and HealthKit sleep bounds.
types: ImportDataView.ParsedImportFile: enum — flowHRV / eliteHRV / standardRR parse outcome

flags.text: Only file read/sniff/parse is off the main actor (comment 35-37). ImportDataView is a SwiftUI View (MainActor-isolated; the explicit `nonisolated` on parseFile/readTextContents confirms it), so analyzeImportedData/runAnalysis and the per-session analyzeImportedSession loop run artifact detection, window selection and time/nonlinear/frequency analysis on the main actor; a multi-night Emuqu export blocks the UI between Task.yield() calls for each full-night analysis.
runAnalysis and importedAnalysis are the same window-bounds + time/nonlinear/frequency + assembleResult pipeline, differing only in how failure is surfaced (failAnalysis vs log).
No unit tests exercise ImportDataView's import/batch logic (only ImportSleepWindowTests for the helper and snapshot tests rendering the empty screen).

branches.effect: continue to URL guard
return silently with state reset and no error shown; otherwise isImporting=true and loadFile Task launched
log error and set errorMessage to its localizedDescription

units.does: Sets status 'Opening file', parses the file in a detached userInitiated task, then dispatches: Emuqu export → showFlowHRV, Elite summary → showEliteHRV, otherwise parseStandardRR (which re-reads and parses the file). Any thrown error is logged and shown with status 'Import failed' and isImporting cleared.

showEliteHRV(result)
await parseStandardRR(at:) (may throw into the catch)
log, set errorMessage=localizedDescription, isImporting=false, status 'Import failed'

flags.text: For a plain RR file the content is read and decoded twice: once in readTextContents for sniffing, then again by RRDataImporter.importFile (which re-opens the security scope, re-reads and parses).

branches.cond: first line matches Elite HRV summary columns
branches.effect: parse as Elite summary and return .eliteHRV; otherwise return .standardRR

units.does: Nonisolated: opens the security-scoped URL, reads Data, decodes UTF-8 and returns the string; throws fileNotFound if scope access is denied, unreadableFile on read or decode failure (each logged).

branches.effect: log and throw ImportError.fileNotFound; otherwise continue with stopAccessing deferred
log and throw ImportError.unreadableFile (original error replaced)
log and throw ImportError.unreadableFile; otherwise log byte count and return the text

flags.text: Non-UTF-8 exports (e.g. UTF-16 or Latin-1 CSV from Windows tools) are rejected outright as unreadable with no encoding fallback.

units.does: Logs the export stats, computes and stores flowNewSessions (archive dedup), stores flowHRVResult, clears isImporting and sets status 'Ready to import N sessions' with N = all sessions in the file.

flags.text: Status line says 'Ready to import <total> sessions' using flowResult.sessions.count while the button imports only flowNewSessions (already-archived ones excluded), so the two numbers disagree when the file overlaps the archive; the @State comment says the button count and the import should agree.

units.does: Logs, filters the Elite summaries to those with no archive entry within 1 h of their date into eliteNewSessions, stores eliteHRVResult, clears isImporting and sets status 'Ready to import <total> sessions'.

flags.text: Import dedup uses SessionArchive.sessionExists(for:), which matches ANY archive entry (any session type, including workouts) whose start is within 1 h, while single-reading save uses holdsCopy (same type + overlapping span). An imported overnight that starts within an hour of an archived workout or nap is hidden as 'already imported' and never offered; a genuine copy starting >1 h apart is offered and then merged/skipped by archiveBatch.
Status says 'Ready to import <total> sessions' (all sessions) while the button counts only eliteNewSessions.

units.does: Sets status 'Parsing RR intervals...', calls RRDataImporter.importFile (re-reads, detects JSON/CSV/Kubios/TXT, validates ≥60 beats and plausible RR), logs, stores importResult, clears isImporting, sets status 'File loaded - N beats'. Throws importer errors to loadFile.

Single-file analysis: builds an HRVSession from importResult, detects artifacts, selects the best window (no sleep bounds), runs time/nonlinear/frequency analysis, attaches window metadata, marks the session complete with recoveryScore nil, then presentResults. Fails with an on-screen message when there is no RR series or not enough clean data.

branches.effect: return silently; otherwise set isAnalyzing and continue
log 0 points
failAnalysis('Analysis failed - no RR data') and return
return (error already surfaced by runAnalysis); otherwise continue
copy window provenance onto the result; otherwise result has no window metadata

flags.text: A plain-text RR file carries no date, so RRDataImporter.createSession dates the session Date() (now). The imported reading is therefore saved as a session starting at import time: it shows as today's reading and feeds the baseline in today's position regardless of when it was recorded.

units.does: Loads up to MorningResultsView.recentSessionsContextLimit (28) overnight sessions before the imported session's start off-main, then sets importedSession, cachedRecentSessions, clears isAnalyzing, status 'Analysis complete', and shows the results cover.
MainActor: clears batch spinner/progress, sets errorMessage and status 'Import failed'.
Logs the line, sets errorMessage and clears isAnalyzing.

flags.text: Does not reset importStatusMessage, so after a failed analysis the status card keeps the last progress text (e.g. 'Running HRV analysis...') next to the error card.

units.does: Computes time-domain and nonlinear metrics over the window (or whole series when no window), surfaces 'insufficient clean data' via failAnalysis and returns nil if either is nil, else returns assembleResult with frequency-domain metrics.

branches.effect: windowStart = 0
windowEnd = series.points.count (whole series)
fail with 'insufficient clean data', return nil; otherwise build result

units.does: Static: collects clean RR (non-artifact) in the window, computes window artifact percentage, and builds HRVAnalysisResult with stress index and respiration rate from clean RR; PNS/SNS/readiness/nocturnal fields nil; analysisDate now.

flags.text: Imported readings are scored by a hand-built result, not the live pipeline the comments promise ('Reuses the same pipeline as live recordings', 'The same analysis pipeline overnight recordings use'): ANSMetrics gets pnsIndex, snsIndex, readinessScore, nocturnalHRDip, daytimeRestingHR and nocturnalMedianHR all nil, while HRVAnalysisPipeline.computeANSMetrics computes them; overnight HR stats (attachOvernightHRStats) are never attached. Imported nights therefore show no PNS/SNS/readiness/nocturnal HR figures that a live night of the same data would have. HRVAnalysisPipeline's own comment says copies of this core 'had drifted'.

Re-implements HRVAnalysisPipeline.rangeResult (frequency domain, artifact percentage over the window, clean-beat count, HRVAnalysisResult assembly) and ArtifactDetector.artifactPercentage instead of calling them.

units.does: Logs success, RMSSD and clean-beat count.

Saves importedSession through RRCollector.saveImportedSession (rejects unanalysed and duplicate copies, archives, uploads to iCloud, updates baseline, signals archive change); on success closes the cover and dismisses the sheet, on failure shows the mapped error and closes the cover.

flags.text: unchanged = total - processed counts every session archiveBatch did not write or merge, including ones dropped because the existing copy failed to read or re-write (mergeIntoExisting logs and drops), so the screen reports 'All N sessions already up to date' / 'already up to date' and auto-dismisses when sessions were in fact lost.

units.does: Per-session Emuqu import: fetches HealthKit sleep bounds, builds the session from raw RR, detects artifacts, picks the best window inside sleep, runs the analysis, attaches window metadata, marks complete with recoveryScore nil. Returns nil (logged) on no series or insufficient clean data.

return nil

flags.text: No branch on session type: createSessionFromFlowHRVData keeps the exported session_type (.workout, .nap, ...), yet every session is sent through the overnight path, a HealthKit sleep fetch and a WindowSelector recovery window bounded by sleep, so an imported workout gets a sleep-window recovery analysis.

units.does: Computes the recording end from the RR sum, asks HealthKitManager.fetchSleepData for that span and converts to offsets; on any error logs and returns (nil,nil) (full recording treated as sleep).

branches.effect: log 'could not read sleep data', return (nil,nil); the error itself is discarded

flags.text: HealthKit errors (denied auth, locked device) are swallowed by try? and the session is analysed with the whole recording as sleep; only the debug log records it, the user sees no indication.

log wake time
log that the full recording is used as the sleep period

flags.text: Never sets result.isConsolidated (the pipeline's copy does, HRVAnalysisPipeline.swift:157), so every imported analysis has isConsolidated == nil; AnalysisSummaryGenerator reads `isConsolidated ?? false`, so every imported night is interpreted as a non-consolidated window, and BaselineTracker stores the nil value for its comparisons.
